record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: In random matrix models with external parameters p and critical values p_c where the equilibrium measure changes its nature, can one rigorously analyze the double-scaling regime p→p_c together with matrix size n→∞, and more generally the relevant multi-scaling limits?

evidence.quote: The double-scaling problems, p → pc and matrix size n → ∞, are of basic interest. Most of these problems remain open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a family of unitary-invariant random matrix ensembles on the space of N×N Hermitian matrices with joint eigenvalue density proportional to

   ∏_{i<j} (x_i − x_j)^2 · ∏_i e^{−N V(x_i; p)} dx_1 ··· dx_N,

where V(x; p) is a real-analytic confining potential depending smoothly on an external parameter p in some parameter space P. For each p, let μ_p denote the associated equilibrium measure, i.e. the unique minimizer of the logarithmic energy functional

   I_V(μ) = ∫∫ log(1/|x−y|) dμ(x) dμ(y) + ∫ V(x; p) dμ(x)

among Borel probability measures on R. Call p_c ∈ P a critical value if the support and/or local behavior of the density of μ_p changes nature at p = p_c (for example, a new cut is born, two cuts merge, the density acquires a higher-order zero in the interior, or the density vanishes faster than a square root at an endpoint).

Problem. Develop a rigorous asymptotic description of the eigenvalue statistics in the double-scaling regime in which p → p_c and N → ∞ simultaneously along arbitrary scaling rays (p − p_c) N^α → const, for the appropriate exponent α attached to the type of criticality. More generally, when several scaling parameters are present, rigorously analyze the corresponding multi-scaling limits: determine the limiting local correlation kernels, prove their universality among potentials V with the same type of criticality, and identify the resulting special-function kernels (e.g. kernels constructed from Painlevé transcendents) governing the transition.
artifact.category_tag: Double-scaling limits in random matrix theory
artifact.status_search_result: Several specific double-scaling regimes have been rigorously analyzed via Riemann–Hilbert/steepest-descent methods: birth-of-a-cut transitions (Mo; Eynard), interior critical points with quadratic vanishing leading to Painlevé II kernels (Bleher–Its; Claeys–Kuijlaars and collaborators), and higher-order edge singularities producing Painlevé hierarchies. Universality results for broad classes of potentials at such critical points have been established. However, the general program — covering all types of criticality, all multi-scaling limits, and full universality — remains incomplete, so the overall question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Riemann–Hilbert Approach to Double Scaling Limit of Random Matrix Eigenvalues Near the 'Birth of a Cut' Transition
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotics of the correlation kernel near the singular point where a new cut emerges, obtained via the Riemann–Hilbert approach.

status_evidence.title: Universality of the double scaling limit in random matrix models (Claeys–Kuijlaars)
status_evidence.snippet: Universality at an interior critical point where the density vanishes quadratically is established in a double-scaling limit, with limiting kernels built from Painlevé II.
status_evidence.claim: Universality for the interior quadratic critical case is proved.

status_evidence.title: Phase Transitions and Equilibrium Measures in Random Matrix Models
status_evidence.snippet: Classification and analysis of phase transitions of equilibrium measures in unitary-invariant ensembles.
status_evidence.claim: Phase transitions of equilibrium measures and their critical types have been classified.

status_evidence.title: Double scaling limit in the random matrix model: The Riemann–Hilbert approach (Bleher–Its)
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous Riemann–Hilbert analysis of a double-scaling limit for a quartic ensemble.
status_evidence.claim: At least one prototypical double-scaling problem is rigorously solved.
